article_title: Processing and public access to official documents

test_cases.question: Which bodies may disclose personal data contained in official documents in order to reconcile public access with data protection?
test_cases.answer: Personal data in official documents may be disclosed by: (1) a public authority; (2) a public body; or (3) a private body, but only when that private body holds the documents for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest.
test_cases.supporting_quote: Personal data in official documents held by a public authority or a public body or a private body for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest may be disclosed by the authority or body
key_phrases: task carried out in the public interest

test_cases.question: Under what conditions can personal data in official documents be disclosed?
test_cases.answer: Personal data in official documents may be disclosed in accordance with Union or Member State law to which the public authority or body is subject. The disclosure must be made to reconcile public access to official documents with the right to the protection of personal data pursuant to this Regulation.
test_cases.supporting_quote: may be disclosed by the authority or body in accordance with Union or Member State law to which the public authority or body is subject in order to reconcile public access to official documents with the right to the protection of personal data pursuant to this Regulation
key_phrases: in accordance with Union or Member State law

test_cases.question: Do the rules on public access to official documents cover all personal data held by a public body?
test_cases.answer: No. This article specifically applies only to personal data contained within official documents. It does not cover all personal data held by the body - only data that is part of official documents held for public access purposes.
test_cases.supporting_quote: Personal data in official documents held by a public authority

coverage.86 entities: Test case 1 - Public authority, public body, private body with public interest
coverage.86 conditions: Test case 2 - In accordance with EU/MS law, to reconcile access with DP
coverage.86 scope: Test case 3 - Only personal data IN official documents

b2b_relevance: LOW - Article 86 primarily affects public authorities and bodies subject to freedom of information laws. B2B SaaS relevance: (1) If you process data for government clients, understand FOI may override some DP rights, (2) If you're a private body performing public interest tasks (e.g., public utility contracts), official documents may be disclosable. This is about government transparency, not typical B2B data processing.
